node.title: REQUIRED LEMMA (QA21-G1): the per-pair dihedral-aligned support cap
node.statement: For a fixed pair (u,v), bound the number of simultaneously-aligned inversion-closed supports: the dihedral analogue of the tangent staircase. QA.21 shows the crude bound (all N_dih = 2 C((n-2)/2, (j-1)/2) supports) blows the clean-rate budget by +52..+292 bits (Row C) — the allowance survives only if per-pair dihedral simultaneity is suppressed by those factors. STRUCTURAL HANDLES: (a) every odd-j inversion-closed support contains one of exactly TWO points ({+1, -1}) — all dihedral-aligned supports pass through one of two links, so the top-core/link machinery bites maximally; (b) palindromic agreement rigidity (the aligned word's symmetric part is constrained); (c) E25's toy data shows small per-pair counts empirically (100/64 charged events across the whole corpus). Expected shape: linear-in-n like the tangent staircase.
node.attack_surface: start from the fixed-point observation: condition on the support containing +1; the aligned family through one point at one slope is a moving-root-type family — the tangent staircase argument should transfer nearly verbatim; E25's charging machinery is the toy calibration
node.falsifier: a toy pair aligning super-linear-in-n dihedral supports (searchable with E25's machinery)
node.notes: GPT PRO X-3 + Codex integration (verifier 36/36): PROVED in the deep regime 3j <= n-k — at most n+2 exact supports across ALL slopes, dihedrality not even needed (two supports pin (U,V); third codewords forced to the pencil; error-word zero sets change at <= n slopes). HONESTLY SCOPED: not applicable at the clean-rate candidates (j ~ 957 of 1024).
